subject: HealthGrid onboarding: PII mapping, subprocessors & data flow deliverables
messages:
From: Alicia Gomez <alicia.gomez@healthgrid.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: privacy@healthgrid.com
Date: Tue, 23 May 2028 16:03:00 -05:00
Subject: Onboarding intake — PII mapping, subprocessors, and transfer controls

Hi Marissa —

Thanks for the intro last week. As part of our onboarding checklist we need a couple items to finish HealthGrid's internal privacy review and procurement sign-off:

1) A concise PII classification matrix for the services we will use (examples: name, DOB, device identifiers, health-related free text) mapping where data is processed/stored and any tokenization/pseudonymization you apply.
2) Current subprocessor roster and the location (region) of data handling for each.
3) A simple data flow diagram showing ingress, encryption-in-transit/rest, KMS custody, and any transient egress to external analytics or partner services.
4) Confirmation of whether Redwood performs any full-text retention of customer inputs and the retention window for short-term caches vs permanent storage.

Can you please provide these artifacts or a timeline for delivery? We aim to complete our privacy gating by May 31. If helpful, I can share our template.

Regards,
Alicia Gomez
Senior Privacy Manager — HealthGrid
Alicia.Gomez@healthgrid.com

---
Note: We are happy to accept redacted diagrams or pointers to hosted docs if there are size/NDAs to consider.

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 24 May 2028 08:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Onboarding intake — PII mapping, subprocessors, and transfer controls

Marissa / Ben — attaching the artifacts below. I generated a concise PII classification matrix (sheet 1) that maps fields to processing layers (ingest, runtime memory/KV cache, persistent logs) and included notes on default pseudonymization (tokenization available as an option during ingestion).

Attachments (stubs):
- redwood_pii_dataflow_v2.pdf (data flow diagram with ingress, streaming runtime cache, KMS custody lines, and third-party analytics egress flagged)
- subprocessor_roster_202805.xlsx (current roster with region column and contract status)
- kms_key_rotation_policy.txt (summary of rotation cadence and customer-managed KMS options)

Quick answers to HealthGrid questions inline:
- Full-text retention: by default Redwood retains customer inputs only for transient KV/cache to support streaming and responses; persisted logs are redacted and retained per customer-configured retention (default 90 days for trial accounts, longer with contract). We can offer shorter retention and full redaction on a per-account basis.
- Tokenization: available as an ingestion pipeline stage (customer-configurable). If enabled, PII fields are tokenized before hitting runtime caches.
- Subprocessors: roster includes cloud infra providers, telemetry pipeline vendor, and a managed embeddings provider. Regions are declared in the roster; we have EU/US/APAC tagging.

Ben — can you confirm whether HealthGrid wants customer-managed KMS? If so we should note a one-week ops lead time for key handover and HSM attestation.

Laura
Privacy & Controls Lead
Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alicia Gomez <alicia.gomez@healthgrid.com>
Date: Wed, 24 May 2028 09:16:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Onboarding intake — PII mapping, subprocessors, and transfer controls

Hi Alicia —

Thanks for the checklist. Attached are the artifacts Laura prepared and a short summary of answers to your numbered items. I've included Drive links to the native diagrams so your team can zoom and comment.

Summary answers:
1) PII classification matrix: attached (sheet 1). We map each field to processing scope: ingest, transient runtime cache (seconds–minutes), and persistent logs. By default we do NOT persist full request text beyond transient caches unless you opt into longer retention for debugging/analytics.
2) Subprocessor roster: attached and includes region and contract-level information. No subprocessors have unrestricted cross-border access; region tags indicate where primary handling occurs.
3) Data flow diagram: redwood_pii_dataflow_v2.pdf + Drive link show KMS custody (customer-managed KMS supported), TLS in transit, AES-256 at rest, and explicit egress paths to analytics partners (flagged).
4) Retention: default transient cache for runtime is short-lived (configurable); permanent logs are redacted by default and retention is set per contract (we typically propose 90 days unless the customer requests otherwise).

Next steps: if HealthGrid wants customer-managed KMS, confirm and we will schedule key provisioning (approx. 1 week ops lead time) and supply an HSM attestation. Also happy to walk through the diagram — propose a 30-min sync Thursday if that helps.

Drive links: https://drive.google.com/redwood/healthgrid/pii-dataflow-v2
HubSpot: HS-4521

Best,
Marissa Cole
Sr. Customer Solutions (Onboarding)
Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com
